translations.text: Solomon son of David grew strong in his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.
And Solomon spoke to all Israel—to the commanders of thousands, the commanders of hundreds, the judges, and all the leaders of the clans.
And Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, where the tent of testimony of God was, which Moses, the Lord’s servant, had made in the wilderness.
But David had brought the ark of God up from the city of Kiriath-jearim, for David had prepared a tent for it in Jerusalem.
And the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the Lord’s tent, and Solomon himself and the assembly sought it.
And Solomon offered there on the bronze altar before the Lord at the tent, and he presented a thousand burnt offerings on it.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask what I should give you.”
And Solomon said to God, “You showed great mercy to David my father, and you made me king in his place.
And now, Lord God, may your name prove faithful concerning David my father, for you have made me king over this numerous people, who are like the dust of the earth.
And now give me wisdom and understanding, so that I may go out and come in before this people of yours, for who can judge this great people of yours?”

And God said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for abundant possessions, or glory, or the lives of your enemies, and did not ask for many days, but asked for wisdom and understanding for yourself so that you might judge my people, over whom I made you king,
I give you wisdom and understanding. I will also give you greatness, possessions, and glory, such that no king before you has been like you, and none after you will be so.”
And Solomon came from Bamah in Gibeon to Jerusalem, from before the tent of testimony, and he reigned over Israel.

And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the cities of the horsemen, while the army was with the king in Jerusalem.
And the king made gold and silver as plentiful as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars in Judea as plentiful as sycamore trees in the plain.
And Solomon’s horses came from Egypt, and the king’s merchants went and bought them at a price.

They brought up a chariot from Egypt for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty. In the same way, through their hands they brought them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of the Syrians.
And Solomon ordered that a house be built for the name of the Lord and a house for his kingdom.
And Solomon gathered seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains, and thirty-six hundred overseers over them.
And Solomon sent word to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, “Just as you dealt with David my father and gave him cedar timber to build himself a house to live in,

so now, behold, I, his son, am building a house for the name of the Lord my God, to consecrate it to him, to burn incense before him, to set out bread continually, and to offer burnt offerings regularly, morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the festivals of our God. This is to be done forever in Israel.
And the house that I am building is great, for our God is greater than all gods.
And who can build a house for him, since heaven and the highest heavens cannot contain his glory? And who am I to build him a house, except as a place to burn incense before him?

And now send me a skilled man who knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, in purple, crimson, blue, and fine linen, and who knows how to engrave, to work with my skilled men in Judea and Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.”
And have cedar, cypress, and almug wood brought to me from Lebanon, for I know that no one knows how to cut timber in Lebanon as your servants do. Now let your servants go with my servants
to prepare a great quantity of timber for me, for the house that I am building is great and glorious.

And for the workers who cut the timber, your servants, I have provided food rations: twenty thousand cors of wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand measures of wine, and twenty thousand measures of oil.
And Hiram king of Tyre replied in writing and sent it to Solomon: “Because the Lord loves his people, he has made you king over them.”

And Hiram said, “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who gave King David a wise son endowed with understanding and wisdom, who will build the Lord’s house and a royal house for himself.
And now, I have sent you a wise man endowed with understanding, Hiram my servant.

His mother is one of the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, and how to weave purple, blue, fine linen, and scarlet, how to carve carvings, and how to devise every design that you assign him, together with your skilled craftsmen and the skilled craftsmen of my lord David, your father.
And now let my lord give his servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine that he promised.
And we will cut timber in Lebanon according to all your needs and bring it to you by sea in rafts to Joppa, and you will take it up to Jerusalem.”
And Solomon gathered all the foreigners in Jerusalem, after the census that his father David had taken of them, and they were found to number one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
And he appointed seventy thousand of them as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters, and three thousand six hundred as overseers over them.

And Solomon began to build the Lord’s house in Jerusalem, in the mountains of the Amorites, where the Lord had appeared to his father David, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
And he began to build in the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
And Solomon began to build the house of God, with a length of sixty cubits according to the earlier measure, and a width of twenty cubits.
And the porch in front of the house was twenty cubits long, corresponding to the width of the house, and one hundred twenty cubits high. He overlaid its interior with pure gold.
And he paneled the great hall with cedar wood and overlaid it with pure gold, and carved palm trees and chainwork on it.
And he adorned the house with precious stones for splendor, and with pure gold from Seppharim.
And he overlaid the house with gold, including the walls, the doorposts, the ceiling, and the doors, and carved cherubim on the walls.
And he made the chamber of the Holy of Holies, twenty cubits long along the front side and twenty cubits wide, and overlaid it with pure gold for the cherubim, using six hundred talents.
And the weight of each individual nail was fifty shekels of gold, and he overlaid the upper chamber with gold.
And he made two crafted cherubim in the chamber of the Holy of Holies and overlaid them with gold.
And the wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long: one wing, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and the other wing, five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub.
One wing of the other cherub, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub.
And the wings of the cherubim were spread out over twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
And he made the curtain of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and wove cherubim into it.
And he made two pillars in front of the house, thirty-five cubits high, with capitals five cubits high.
He made latticework in the inner sanctuary and placed it on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments and placed them on the chainwork.
He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and the other on the left. He named the one on the right Uprightness and the one on the left Strength.
He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
He made the cast metal sea, ten cubits across, circular all around, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference.
Beneath it were figures of oxen, surrounding it for ten cubits. They cast the oxen along with the casting itself.
They made them as twelve oxen: three faced north, three faced west, three faced south, and three faced east. The sea rested on them, and their hindquarters were underneath.
The sea was a span thick, and its rim was like the rim of a cup, carved in the form of a lily blossom. It held three thousand measures, and he completed it.
He made ten basins and placed five on the right and five on the left, to wash and rinse in them the things used for burnt offerings. The sea was for the priests to wash themselves in.
He made ten gold lampstands according to their prescribed design and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He also made a hundred gold bowls.
He made the court of the priests, the great court, and the doors of the court, and covered their doors with bronze.
He placed the sea at the right-hand corner of the temple, toward the east, at the front.
Hiram made the meat hooks, the pots, the grates for the altar, and all its equipment. Hiram finished making all the work that King Solomon had commanded for the house of God.
The two pillars, the capitals above them, the two capitals above the capitals of the pillars, and the two latticeworks to cover the capitals that were on top of the pillars;
and four hundred gold bells on the two latticeworks, and two rows of pomegranate-shaped ornaments on each latticework to cover the two capitals that were above the pillars;
And he made ten stands and placed the basins on the stands.
and the one sea, and twelve oxen beneath it;
and the grates, the shovels, the pots, the meat hooks, and all their equipment, which Hiram made and brought to King Solomon for the house of the Lord, all of pure bronze.
The king cast these in the plain of the Jordan, in the thick earth, in the house of Succoth and between Zarethan.
Solomon made all these utensils in very great quantities, for there was no shortage in the weight of bronze.
Solomon made all the utensils for the house of the Lord, the gold altar, and the other tables, with the bread of the Presence upon them;
and the lampstands and their lamps, to give light according to the prescribed arrangement before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold;
and their lamp holders;
and their tongs, the bowls, the incense vessels, and the censers, of pure gold; and the doors of the inner house leading into the Holy of Holies, and the gold doors of the temple.

All the work that Solomon did in the house of the Lord was completed. Solomon brought in the things that his father David had dedicated, and placed the silver, the gold, and the utensils in the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, all the leaders of the tribes, and the heads of the families of the Israelites in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David, which is Zion.
And every man of Israel gathered before the king at the festival, which was in the seventh month.
And all the elders of Israel came, and all the Levites took up the ark.
And they brought it up, along with the tent of testimony and all the sacred utensils that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.

And King Solomon and all the people of Israel, including those who feared God and those assembled with them, were before the ark, sacrificing cattle and sheep that could not be counted or numbered because there were so many.
And the Levites brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord inside to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
The cherubim had their wings spread over the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its carrying poles from above.

The carrying poles extended outward, and the ends of the poles could be seen from the sanctuary in front of the inner sanctuary, but they were not visible from outside. And they remained there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the children of Israel as they came out of the land of Egypt.
And when the priests came out of the sanctuary—for all the priests who were present there had consecrated themselves, and those serving had not been assigned day by day—

all the Levite singers, from the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, and from their sons and brothers, were dressed in fine linen robes and stood on the east side of the altar with harps, lyres, and flutes. With them were one hundred and twenty priests blowing trumpets.

And the trumpet playing, the singing of the psalm, and the raising of their voices became one sound as they said together, “Give thanks and bless the Lord.” And they raised their voices with the trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, and said, “Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.” And the house was filled with the cloud of the Lord’s glory.
And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.
Then Solomon said, “The Lord said that he would dwell in thick darkness.”
And I built a house for your name, your sanctuary, and prepared it for you to dwell in forever.
And the king turned his face and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood around him.
And he said, “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who spoke with his own mouth to David my father and fulfilled it with his own hands.

And he said, ‘From the day when I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city from all the tribes of Israel in which to build myself a house, so that my name would be there, and I chose no man to be ruler over my people Israel.’
“And now I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to rule over my people Israel.”
And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
And the Lord said to David my father, ‘Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well to have this in your heart.
Nevertheless, you shall not build me a house. Instead, your son, who will come from your own body, shall build a house for my name.’

And the Lord fulfilled the word that he had spoken. I succeeded David my father and sat on the throne of Israel, as the Lord had said, and I built this house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
And I placed here the ark of the covenant that he made with the children of Israel.”
And he stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel and raised his hands.

For Solomon made a bronze platform and placed it in the middle of the temple courtyard. It was five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high. He stood on it, fell to his knees before the whole assembly of Israel, and raised his hands toward heaven.
And he said, “Lord, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth. You keep your covenant and show mercy to all who walk before you with all their hearts.”
For you have kept for your servant David my father what you spoke to him and said. You spoke with your mouth and fulfilled it with your hands today.

And now, Lord God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father whatever you spoke to him and said: ‘You shall never lack a man before me to sit on the throne of Israel, provided that your sons guard their ways and walk before me as you walked before me.’
And now, Lord God of Israel, let your word to David prove true.
But will God truly dwell with human beings on earth? For if heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you, what is this house that I have built?
And now, Lord God, attend to your servant’s prayer and my requests, to hear the plea and the prayer that your servant offers before you today.
May your eyes and your mind be open toward this house day and night, toward this place where you said your name would be invoked, to hear the prayer that your servant offers in this place.
And hear the requests of your servant and your people Israel, whatever they pray in this place. Hear from your dwelling place, from heaven; hear and forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath invoking a curse upon himself because of it, and comes and stands before this altar in this house,

then hear from heaven, act, and judge your servants, repaying the lawless man by bringing his conduct upon his own head, vindicating the righteous man, and giving each person according to his righteousness.
“And if your people Israel are defeated by their enemies because they have sinned against you, and they turn back, acknowledge your name, pray, and plead before you in this house,”
Then hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that you gave them and their fathers.
When you shut up the heavens so that there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray in this place, praise your name, and turn from their sins because you humble them,

then hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your servants and your people Israel, for you will show them the good way in which they should walk. Give rain upon your land, which you gave your people as an inheritance.

If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence, scorching blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, if an enemy oppresses them before their cities, whatever the plague and whatever the disease,
whatever prayer and whatever supplication any person or all your people Israel may offer, if a person recognizes his own leprosy and his own affliction and raises his hands toward this house,
then hear from heaven, from your established dwelling place, and heal. Give each person according to his heart, as you know his heart, for you alone know the hearts of human beings,
so that they may fear your ways all the days that they live on the face of the land that you gave their fathers.
And every foreigner who is not of your people Israel and comes from a distant land because of your great name, your mighty hand, and your uplifted arm—when they come and pray in this place,

And hear from heaven, from your established dwelling place, and do everything the foreigner calls upon you to do, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and may know that your name is invoked over this house that I have built.
If your people go out to war against their enemies by the way you send them, and pray to you facing this city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
then hear their pleas and their prayers from heaven, and uphold their cause.

For they will sin against you—since there is no one who does not sin—and you will strike them and hand them over to their enemies, and they will be taken captive to the land of their enemies, to a land far away or nearby.
And if they turn back in their hearts in the land to which they were taken, and return and plead with you in their captivity, saying, “We have sinned and acted lawlessly,”

“And they return to you with all their hearts and with their whole being in the land of their captivity, and pray toward this land that you gave their ancestors, toward the city that you chose, and toward the house that I built for your name,”
then hear their prayers and their pleas from heaven, from your established dwelling place, and uphold their cause, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
And now, Lord, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the pleas made in this place.
And now arise, Lord God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your holiness. Let your priests, Lord God, be clothed with salvation, and let your children rejoice in good things.
Lord God, do not turn your face away from your anointed one. In your mercy, remember David your servant.
And when Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
And the priests could no longer enter the house of the Lord at that time, because the glory of the Lord filled the house.

And all the Israelites saw the fire descending and the glory of the Lord over the house. They fell facedown to the ground on the stone pavement, worshiped, and praised the Lord: “For he is good, for his mercy endures forever.”
And the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the Lord.
And Solomon offered as sacrifices twenty-two thousand bulls and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep from the pastures. And the king and all the people dedicated the temple of God.

And the priests stood at their assigned duties, and the Levites with musical instruments for the songs of the Lord and of King David, to give thanks before the Lord, “For his mercy endures forever,” with David’s praises performed through them. And the priests sounded trumpets before them, and all Israel stood.

And Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard that was at the house of the Lord, because there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings. For the bronze altar that Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the fat.
And Solomon celebrated the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance to Hamath to the torrent valley of Egypt.
And on the eighth day he held a closing assembly, for he had celebrated the dedication of the altar for the seven days of the festival.

And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for all the good things that the Lord had done for David and Solomon and for his people Israel.
And Solomon completed the house of the Lord and the king’s house, and he succeeded in doing everything Solomon desired to do in the house of the Lord and in his own house.
And God appeared to Solomon that night and said to him, “I have heard your prayers. I have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.”
If I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, and if I command the locusts to devour the trees, and if I send pestilence among my people,
and if my people, over whom my name is called, are ashamed and pray and seek my face and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven and forgive them and heal their land.
And now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
And now, behold, I have chosen this house and made it holy so that my name may be here forever, and my eyes and my heart will be here always.
And you, if you walk before me as David your father did, and do everything that I commanded you, and keep my decrees and my judgments,
I will establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, ‘You will never lack a man to rule in Israel.’
But if you turn away and abandon my decrees and my commandments, which I have set before you, and go and serve foreign gods and bow down to them,
I will remove you from this land that I gave you, and this house, which I made holy for my name, I will cast away from my presence and make it a proverb and a tale among all nations.
And this lofty house—everyone who passes by it will be astonished and say, ‘Why has the Lord done this to this land and this house?’

And they will say, “Because they abandoned the Lord, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and accepted foreign gods, bowed down to them, and served them. That is why he brought all these disasters upon them.”
And it happened after twenty years, during which Solomon built the house of the Lord and his own house,
that Solomon rebuilt the cities that Hiram had given him and settled the Israelites there.
And Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and strengthened it.
And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and he built all the fortified cities in Hamath.
And he built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon as fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars,

and Baalath, and all the fortified cities belonging to Solomon, and all the cities for chariots and all the cities for horses, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and throughout his kingdom.
All the people who remained from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not Israelites,
but were descendants of those who remained with them in the land, whom the Israelites had not destroyed—Solomon made them pay tribute, as they do to this day.
But Solomon did not take any Israelites as servants for his kingdom, because they were warriors, commanders of the troops, and commanders of the chariots and horsemen.
And these were the chief officers of Solomon’s kingdom: two hundred and fifty, who supervised the people.

And Solomon brought Pharaoh’s daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, because he said, ‘My wife must not live in the city of David, king of Israel, because the place where the ark of the Lord entered is holy.’
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the Lord on his altar, which he had built in front of the temple,

offering them according to each day’s requirements, as Moses had commanded, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the festivals three times a year: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths.

And according to David’s ordinances, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service, and the Levites for their duties, to give praise and serve before the priests as required each day, and the gatekeepers according to their divisions at each gate, for this was the command of David, the man of God.
And they did not depart from the king’s command concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter or concerning the treasuries.
All the work was completed, from the day it began until the day Solomon finished the house of the Lord.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Elath, which was on the seacoast of Judea.

Hiram sent ships through his servants, along with men who knew how to sail the sea. They went with Solomon’s servants to Ophir, took four hundred and fifty talents of gold from there, and came to King Solomon.

The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon’s fame and came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with riddles, bringing a very large retinue and camels laden with incense, much gold, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke with him about everything that was on her mind.
Solomon explained all her questions to her. There was not a single matter beyond Solomon that he did not explain to her.
The queen of Sheba saw Solomon’s wisdom and the house he had built,

the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the arrangement of his attendants and their robes, his cupbearers and their clothing, and the burnt offerings he offered in the house of the Lord. She was astonished and said to the king,
“The report I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom was true.
But I did not believe the reports until I came and my own eyes saw it. Look, they did not tell me even half of the abundance of your wisdom. You have surpassed the report I heard.
Happy are your men, and happy are your women and these servants of yours who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom.

Blessed be the Lord your God, who was pleased with you and placed you on the throne of his kingdom over your people. Because the Lord your God loved Israel and wished to establish it forever, he made you king over them to administer justice and righteousness.”
She gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, a very great quantity of incense, and precious stones. There was no incense like that which the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
Solomon’s servants and Hiram’s servants brought Solomon gold from Ophir, as well as cypress wood and precious stones.
The king made the cypress wood into steps for the house of the Lord and the king’s house, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Nothing like this had ever been seen before in the land of Judah.
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired and requested, apart from what she had given King Solomon. Then she returned to her own land.
The weight of the gold brought to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
apart from what the appointed men and the merchants brought. Gold and silver were also brought to King Solomon from all the kingdoms of the Arabs and from the governors of the land.
King Solomon made three hundred shields of hammered gold, using six hundred gold coins of pure gold for each shield,
and three hundred spears of hammered gold, using three hundred gold coins for each spear. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a large throne of ivory and covered it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps bound with gold, and armrests on either side of the seat. Two lions stood beside the feet of the armrests.
Twelve lions stood on either side of the six steps. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom.
All King Solomon’s utensils were made of gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were studded with gold. Silver was considered of no value in Solomon’s days.
For King Solomon’s ship went to Tarshish with Hiram’s servants, and once every three years the king’s ship returned from Tarshish, loaded with gold, silver, elephant tusks, monkeys, and peacocks.
Solomon surpassed all the kings in wealth and wisdom.
And all the kings of the earth sought to see Solomon and hear his wisdom, which God had put into his heart.
Each of them brought him gifts: silver vessels, gold vessels, robes, stacte, incense, horses, and mules, year after year.
Solomon had forty thousand mares for his chariots and twelve thousand riding horses. He placed them in the chariot cities, and they were with Solomon in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and to the borders of Egypt.
And the king made gold and silver as plentiful as stones in Jerusalem, and cedar wood as plentiful as the sycamore trees in the plains.
Solomon’s horses came from Egypt and from every land.

The rest of Solomon’s deeds, from first to last, are written in the accounts of Nathan the prophet, in the accounts of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the vision of Joel the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.
King Solomon reigned over all Israel for forty years.
Solomon fell asleep, and they buried him in the city of David his father. Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
Rehoboam came to Shechem, because all Israel was coming to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard this—he was in Egypt, having fled from King Solomon, and Jeroboam was living in Egypt—Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
They sent for him and summoned him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came to King Rehoboam and said,
“Your father made our yoke harsh. Now ease the harsh service imposed by your father and the heavy yoke he placed on us, and we will serve you.”
He said to them, “Go away for three days, and then come back to me.” And the people went away.
King Rehoboam gathered the elders who had served before Solomon his father while he was alive, and said, “What do you think, and what do you advise me to say in answer to these people?”
They spoke to him and said, “If today you are good to these people, please them, and speak kindly to them, they will be your servants forever.”
He abandoned the advice the elders had given him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and who served before him.
He said to them, “What do you think I should say in answer to these people who spoke to me and said, ‘Lighten the yoke your father placed on us’?”

The young men who had grown up with him spoke to him: “This is what you should say to the people who spoke to you and said, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should lighten it for us.’ Say this: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.’”
“And now, my father disciplined you with a heavy yoke, and I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with rods, and I will discipline you with scorpions.”
Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said: “Return to me on the third day.”
The king answered harshly, and King Rehoboam abandoned the advice of the elders.

He spoke to them according to the advice of the young men and said, “My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to it. My father disciplined you with rods, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”

The king did not listen to the people, because the downfall was from God, and the Lord confirmed his word, which he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat and all Israel. And the king did not listen to them.

The people answered the king and said, “What share do we have in David, or what inheritance in the son of Jesse? Go away to your homes, Israel! Now look after your own house, David!” And all Israel went to their homes.
The men of Israel who remained in the cities of Judah made Rehoboam king over themselves.
King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was in charge of the tribute, and the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam hurried to climb into his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
Israel has spurned the house of David to this day.
Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and gathered Judah and Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand young men who could wage war, to fight against Israel and restore the kingdom to himself.
The word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying:
“Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon and to all Judah and Benjamin, and say:

‘Thus says the Lord: Do not go up or fight against your brothers. Let each person return to his own home, because this thing has come from me.’” They listened to the word of the Lord and turned back, no longer going against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built fortified cities in Judah.
He built Bethlehem, Etam, and Tekoa,
Beth-zur, Soco, and Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, and Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah, and Zorah,
and Aijalon and Hebron, fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin.
He strengthened them with walls and placed commanders in them, along with stores of food, oil, and wine.
He placed shields and spears in each city and made them very strong. Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.
The priests and Levites throughout Israel gathered to him from all its territories.
For the Levites left their homes and estates and went to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had expelled them so that they could no longer serve the Lord.
He appointed his own priests for the high places, the idols, the worthless things, and the calves that Jeroboam had made.

And he brought them out from the tribes of Israel—those who had set their hearts on seeking the Lord, the God of Israel—and they came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the Lord, the God of their ancestors.
They strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and Rehoboam son of Solomon grew strong for three years, because he walked in the ways of David and Solomon for those three years.
Rehoboam took as wives Mahalath daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and Abiad daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
They bore him sons: Jerum, Shemariah, and Zaham.
After this he took Maacah daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines. He had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
Rehoboam appointed Abijah, the son of Maacah, as ruler over his brothers, because he intended to make him king.
He prospered more than all his sons throughout all the territories of Judah and Benjamin, in the fortified cities. He placed very abundant food supplies in them and sought many wives.
When Rehoboam’s kingdom was established and he had grown strong, he abandoned the commandments of the Lord, and all Israel did so with him.
In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned against the Lord.
He had twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and the people who came with him from Egypt were beyond counting: Libyans, Troglodytes, and Ethiopians.
They overpowered the fortified cities in Judah, and he came to Jerusalem.

Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the leaders of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, “Thus says the Lord: You have abandoned me, and I will abandon you into Shishak’s hands.”
The leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, “The Lord is righteous.”

When the Lord saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, “They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them, but will grant them a little deliverance, and my wrath shall not pour down upon Jerusalem.
For they shall become my servants, and they shall learn the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of the earth.”
Shishak king of Egypt came up and took the treasures that were in the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king’s house. He took everything; he also took the gold shields that Solomon had made.
Rehoboam made bronze shields in their place, and Shishak appointed over them the commanders of the couriers who guarded the king’s door.
Whenever the king entered the house of the Lord, the guards and the couriers would also enter, and they would carry them before the couriers.
When he humbled himself, the Lord’s anger turned away from him, and he was not utterly destroyed, because there were good things in Judah.

Rehoboam grew strong in Jerusalem and reigned. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to place his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonite.
He did evil because his heart was not set on seeking the Lord.

Are not the accounts of Rehoboam, from first to last, written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and Iddo the seer, together with his deeds? There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
Rehoboam died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Abijah became king in his place.
In the eighteenth year of Jeroboam’s reign, Abijah became king over Judah and Jerusalem for three years.
His mother’s name was Maacah, daughter of Absalom. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

Abijah drew up his forces for battle with four hundred thousand mighty warriors, and Jeroboam drew up his forces against him for battle with eight hundred thousand mighty men who fought with strength.
Abijah rose up from Mount Zemaraim, which was in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, “Listen, Jeroboam and all Israel!
Should you not know that the Lord, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel to David and his sons forever by a covenant of salt?
And Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
Wicked men, lawless fellows, gathered around him, and he opposed Rehoboam son of Solomon. Rehoboam was young and fainthearted and did not stand against him.
And now you say you will stand against the kingdom of the Lord, which is in the hands of David’s sons. You are very numerous, and with you are the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.

Did you not drive out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and make yourselves priests from the people of the land? Anyone who came to be ordained with a bull from the herd and seven rams became a priest of gods that are not gods.
But we have not abandoned the Lord our God, and his priests who serve the Lord are the sons of Aaron, along with the Levites and those among them who are continually on duty.

They burn incense to the Lord and offer burnt offerings every morning and evening, along with blended incense. The bread of the Presence is on the holy table, and the golden lampstand and its lamps are lit to burn every evening, for we keep the observances of the Lord, the God of our fathers, but you have abandoned him.

“And look, the Lord is with us as our leader, along with his priests and the signal trumpets to sound the signal among us. And you, people of Israel, are you fighting against the Lord, the God of our ancestors? You will no longer succeed.”
And Jeroboam sent the men lying in ambush around to come from behind. His forces were in front of Judah, and the men lying in ambush were behind.
And Judah turned, and behold, the battle was before them and behind them. They cried out to the Lord, and the priests sounded the trumpets.
And the men of Judah shouted, and when the men of Judah shouted, the Lord struck down Jeroboam and Israel before Abijah and Judah.
And the Israelites fled before Judah, and the Lord delivered them into their hands.
And Abijah and his army struck them with a great slaughter, and five thousand mighty men of Israel fell wounded.
And the Israelites were humbled that day, and the people of Judah grew strong because they trusted in the Lord, the God of their fathers.
And Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took cities from him: Bethel and its villages, Anah and its villages, Ephron and its dependent towns, and Bea and its villages.
And Jeroboam never regained his strength throughout the days of Abijah. The Lord struck him, and he died.
And Abijah grew strong and took fourteen wives for himself, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
And the remaining accounts of Abijah, his deeds and his words, are written in the book of the prophet Iddo.
And Abijah died and joined his ancestors, and they buried him in the City of David. His son Asa reigned in his place. In Asa’s days, the land of Judah was at peace for ten years.
And he did what was good and right before the Lord his God.
And he removed the foreign altars and the high places, shattered the pillars, and burned the sacred groves.
And he told Judah to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, and to carry out the law and the commandments.
And he removed the altars and the idols from all the cities of Judah.
And the fortified cities in the land of Judah were at peace, because the land was at peace. He faced no war from any quarter during those years, because the Lord had given him rest.

And he said to Judah, “Let us build these cities and make walls, towers, gates, and bars while we possess this land. For just as we sought the Lord our God, he sought us and gave us rest on every side and made us prosper.”

And Asa had an army of armed men: three hundred thousand from the land of Judah who carried shields and spears, and two hundred and sixty thousand shield-bearers and archers from the land of Benjamin. All of them were mighty warriors.
And Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.
And Asa went out against him, and the battle lines were drawn up in the valley north of Mareshah.

And Asa cried out to the Lord his God and said, “Lord, it is not difficult for you to save through many or through few. Strengthen us, Lord our God, because we have trusted in you, and in your name we have come against this multitude. Lord our God, do not let a human being prevail against you.”
And the Lord struck the Ethiopians before Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.

And Asa and his army pursued them as far as Gedor. The Ethiopians fell until none of them remained alive, for they were crushed before the Lord and before his army. And they took a great deal of plunder.
And they destroyed their villages around Gedor, because terror from the Lord had fallen upon them. They plundered all their cities, for there was much plunder in them.
They also took their livestock tents and slaughtered the [?]. They took many flocks and camels and returned to Jerusalem.
And the Spirit of the Lord came upon Azariah son of Adad.

And he went out to meet Asa and all Judah and Benjamin and said, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The Lord is with you because you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, and if you abandon him, he will abandon you.”
And for many days Israel had no true God, no priest to teach, and no law.
Who brought them back to the Lord, the God of Israel, and was found among them.
At that time there was no peace for those who came in or went out, because terrors from the Lord fell upon all the inhabitants of the lands.
And nation fought against nation and city against city, because God terrified them with every kind of distress.
But now, be strong, and do not let your hands grow weak, for there is a reward for your deeds.”

When he heard these words and the prophecy of Azariah the prophet, he took courage and removed all the abominations from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. And he rededicated the altar of the Lord that stood before the Lord’s temple.

And he assembled Judah and Benjamin, along with the newcomers and foreigners from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who were with him, because many from Israel had joined him when they saw that the Lord their God was with him.
And they gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign.
And on that day they sacrificed to the Lord seven hundred young bulls and seven thousand sheep from the plunder they had brought.
And he established a covenant to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and all their soul.
And whoever would not seek the Lord, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, from the young to the old, both men and women.
And they swore to the Lord with a loud voice and with a horn and a trumpet.
And all Judah rejoiced over the oath, because they had sworn with all their hearts and had sought him with complete willingness. He was found by them, and the Lord gave them rest on every side.
And he removed Maacah his mother because she was a worshiper of Astarte. He smashed the idols and burned them in the Kidron ravine.
Nevertheless, they did not remove the high places, and these still remained in Judah and Israel. But Asa’s heart was wholly devoted throughout all the days of his life.
And he brought in the sacred offerings of David his father and the things dedicated to the Lord God: silver, gold, and utensils.
And he had no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
And in the thirty-eighth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and fortified Ramah, allowing Asa king of Judah no way out.
And Asa took gold and silver from the treasuries of the Lord’s house and from the king’s house and sent them to Ben-Hadad, king of the Syrians, who lived in Damascus, saying:

“Establish a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you silver and gold. Come and drive Baasha king of Israel away from me, so that he will withdraw from me.”
And Ben-Hadad, king of the Syrians, listened and sent the commanders of his forces against the cities of Israel. He struck Aven, Dan, Abel-maim, and the whole area around the region of Naphtali.
And when Baasha heard this, he gave up fortifying Ramah, and his work ceased.
And King Asa brought all Judah and took the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had built, and used them to build Gibeah and Mizpah.

At that time Hanani the prophet came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, “Because you relied on the king of the Syrians and did not rely on the Lord your God, the army of the king of Israel has escaped from your hands.
“Were not the Ethiopians and Libyans a large army? They came boldly, with very many horsemen, yet when you relied on the Lord, the Lord delivered them into your hands.”
For the eyes of the Lord look throughout the whole earth to strengthen all whose hearts are fully devoted to him. But now you have acted foolishly in this matter; from now on you will have war.
Asa became angry with the prophet and put him in prison, because he was enraged over this. Asa also treated the people cruelly at that time.
Now the acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Asa’s feet became diseased in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, and he became very ill. Yet in his illness he did not seek the Lord, but sought physicians.
Asa rested with his fathers and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

They buried him in the tomb he had dug for himself in the city of David. They laid him on a couch and filled it with spices and various kinds of oils prepared by perfumers, and they held a very great funeral for him.
His son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place, and Jehoshaphat strengthened himself against Israel.
He placed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah and appointed governors in all the cities of Ephraim that his father, King Asa, had captured.
The Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he followed the earlier ways of his father and did not seek the idols,
but sought the Lord, the God of his father, and followed his father's commandments. His deeds were not like those of Israel.
The kingdom prospered in his hands, and all Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat. He attained greatness and much glory.
His heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord, and he also removed the high places and the sacred groves from the land of Judah.
In the third year of his reign, he sent his officials and the sons of the mighty men—Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah.
With them were the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jonathan, Adonijah, and Tobadonijah; and with them were the priests Elishama and Jehoram.
They taught in Judah, taking the book of the law of the Lord with them. They went through the cities of Judah and taught the people.
Terror from the Lord fell upon the kings of the lands surrounding Judah, and they did not wage war against Jehoshaphat.

Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts of gold and silver and offerings. The Arabs brought him seven thousand seven hundred rams from their flocks and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
Jehoshaphat continued to grow in greatness, and he built houses in Judea, fortified cities.
He undertook many works in Judea, and there were strong, mighty fighting men in Jerusalem.
This was their number according to their ancestral houses. From Judah, among the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty warriors;
and alongside them, Johanan the commander, and with him two hundred eighty thousand;
and alongside him, Amasiah son of Zechariah, who willingly devoted himself to the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand mighty warriors.
From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty warrior, and with him two hundred thousand archers and slingers;
and alongside them, Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand men strong in battle.
These served the king, besides those whom the king had stationed in the fortified cities throughout Judea.
Jehoshaphat attained greatness and also much glory, and he formed a marriage alliance with the house of Ahab.
At the end of the year he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered many sheep and oxen for him and for the troops who were with him, and urged him to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead.

Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?” He said to him, “As I am, so are you, and my troops are like your troops. We will be with you in battle.”
Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Let us inquire of the Lord today.”

The king of Israel gathered the prophets of Israel, four hundred men, and said to them, “Should I go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or should I refrain?” They said, “Go up, and God will grant success to the king.”
Jehoshaphat said, “Is there not another prophet of the Lord here, so that we may inquire through him?”

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is one more man through whom we can inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good for me, but always disaster. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “Let the king not speak that way.”
The king of Israel called a eunuch and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.”

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were each sitting on his own throne, dressed in robes. They were sitting in the open space at the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself and said, “This is what the Lord says: With these you will strike the Syrians until you destroy them.”
All the prophets were prophesying in the same way, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and you will succeed. The Lord will deliver it into the king’s hands.”

The messenger who went to summon Micaiah spoke to him and said, “Look, the prophets have spoken good things for the king with one voice. Let your words be like those of one of them, and speak good things.”
Micaiah said, “As the Lord lives, whatever God says to me, that is what I will speak.”

He came to the king, and the king said to him, “Micaiah, should I go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or should I refrain?” He said, “Go up, and it will succeed, and they will be delivered into your hands.”
The king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear to speak nothing to me but the truth in the name of the Lord?”
He said, “I saw Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd. The Lord said, ‘They have no ruler. Let each return to his own home in peace.’”
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good things about me, but disaster?”
He said, “Not so! Hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven stood beside him, on his right and on his left.
The Lord said, ‘Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ One said this, and another said that.
Then a spirit came forward, stood before the Lord, and said, ‘I will deceive him.’ The Lord said, ‘How?’
He said, ‘I will go out and become a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ He said, ‘You will deceive him and succeed. Go out and do so.’
And now, look, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken disaster concerning you.”
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came forward, struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said to him, “By what road did the Spirit of the Lord pass through me and speak to you?”
Micaiah said, “You will see on the day when you go from one storeroom to another to hide.”
The king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and bring him back to Shemer, the ruler of this city, and to Joash, the prince, the king’s son.
Say, ‘This is what the king says: Put this man in prison, and let him eat the bread of affliction and drink the water of affliction until I return in peace.’”
Micaiah said, “If you do indeed return in peace, the Lord has not spoken to me. Listen, all you peoples!”
The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Disguise me, and I will enter the battle; but you put on my robe.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered the battle.
The king of the Syrians commanded the chariot commanders who were with him, saying, “Do not fight anyone, small or great, but only the king of Israel.”
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “This is the king of Israel.” They surrounded him to fight, and Jehoshaphat cried out. The Lord saved him, and God turned them away from him.
When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.
A man drew his bow with strength and struck the king of Israel between the lungs and the chest. He said to the eunuch, “Turn your hand and take me out of this battle, for I am wounded.”
The battle was lost that day, and the king of Israel remained on his chariot facing the Syrians until evening. He died at sunset.
Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his house in Jerusalem.

Jehu the prophet, son of Hanani, went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, “Do you help the sinner and befriend someone hated by the Lord? Because of this, wrath from the Lord has come upon you.
But because good things were found in you, because you removed the sacred groves from the land of Judah and directed your heart to seek the Lord, the Lord saved you.”
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
He appointed judges in all the cities of Judah and in the fortified cities, in each city.
He said to the judges, “Consider what you are doing, because you judge not human affairs but the Lord's, and matters of justice are entrusted to you.
Now let the fear of the Lord be upon you. Be watchful and act, for with the Lord our God there is no injustice, partiality, or taking of bribes.”
In Jerusalem Jehoshaphat also appointed some of the priests, Levites, and heads of Israel's ancestral families to judge the inhabitants of Jerusalem according to the Lord's justice.
He commanded them, saying, “Act in this way, with the fear of the Lord, faithfully and wholeheartedly.

For every man, in the cases brought to you by your brothers who live in their cities, between one case of bloodshed and another, and between a matter of law and a commandment, explain the statutes and judgments to them. Let them not sin against God, so that wrath will not come upon you or upon your brothers. Do this, and you will not sin.

Look, Amariah the priest is your chief in every matter concerning the Lord, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, in every matter concerning the king. The scribes and the Levites are before you. Be strong and act, and may the Lord be with the good.”
After this, the Ammonites and the Moabites, together with some of the Meunites, came against Jehoshaphat to wage war.
People came and informed Jehoshaphat, saying, “A great multitude has come against you from beyond the sea, from Syria. They are now at Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi.”
Jehoshaphat was afraid and set himself to seek the Lord. He proclaimed a fast throughout Judah.
Judah assembled to seek the Lord. They came from all the cities of Judah to seek the Lord.
Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah in Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new court,
and said, “Lord, God of our fathers, are you not God in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. In your hand is mighty power, and no one can stand against you.
Are you not the Lord who destroyed the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel and gave it forever to the descendants of Abraham, your beloved?
They lived in it and built a sanctuary here for your name, and said:

If disasters come upon us—sword, judgment, death, or famine—we will stand before this house and before you, for your name is upon this house. We will cry out to you in our distress, and you will hear and save us.

And now, here are the Ammonites, Moabites, and those of Mount Seir, through whose lands you did not allow Israel to pass when they came out of Egypt. Instead, they turned away from them and did not destroy them.
And now, look: they dare to come against us and drive us out of the land of our inheritance, which you gave us.
Lord our God, will you not pass judgment on them? For we have no strength to withstand that great multitude, and we do not know what to do against them. But our eyes are on you.
All Judah stood before the Lord, together with their children and their wives.

The Spirit of the Lord came upon Uzziel, son of Zechariah, of the descendants of Benaiah and of the descendants of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the descendants of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.

He said, “Listen, all Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat! This is what the Lord says to you: Do not be afraid or terrified before that great multitude, for the battle is not yours but God's.
Tomorrow go down against them. Look, they are coming down the slope of Asher, and you will find them beside the river in the wilderness of Jeriel.

It is not for you to fight there. Take heed and see the Lord's deliverance, which is with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or terrified. Tomorrow go down to meet them, for the Lord is with you.”
Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the Lord and worshiped the Lord.
The Levites from the descendants of Kohath and the descendants of Korah rose to praise the Lord God with a loud voice on high.

They rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and called out, saying, “Listen to me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Trust in the Lord our God, and you will be trusted. Trust in his prophets, and you will prosper.”

He consulted with the people and appointed psalm singers and those who offered praise to give thanks and praise the holy things as they went out ahead of the army. They said, “Give thanks to the Lord, for his mercy endures forever.”

When they began to praise the Lord and give thanks to him, the Lord caused the Ammonites to fight against Moab on Mount Seir. These were the people who had come out against Judah, and they were defeated.

The Ammonites and Moabites rose against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to destroy and crush them. When they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they rose against one another to destroy each other.
Judah came to the lookout in the wilderness, looked out, and saw the multitude. There they all lay dead, fallen on the ground, and no one had survived.

Jehoshaphat and the army came to plunder their spoils. They found many livestock, equipment, booty, and valuable vessels, and they carried them off. It took them three days to gather the spoils, because there was so much.
On the fourth day they gathered in the Valley of Blessing, because they blessed the Lord there. For that reason they called that place the Valley of Blessing, as it is called to this day.
Every man of Judah returned to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat leading them, with great joy, because the Lord had made them rejoice over their enemies.
They entered Jerusalem with lyres, harps, and trumpets, and went to the house of the Lord.
Terror from the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the earth when they heard that the Lord had fought against Israel's enemies.
Jehoshaphat’s kingdom was at peace, and his God gave him rest on every side.
Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.
He walked in the ways of his father Asa and did not turn aside from doing what was right before the Lord.
But the high places still remained, and the people did not set their hearts toward the Lord, the God of their fathers.
The rest of the deeds of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the account of Jehu son of Hanani, who wrote the book of the kings of Israel.
After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel.
He acted lawlessly by setting out and going to him and building a ship to sail to Tarshish. He built a ship at Ezion-geber.

Eliezer son of [?], from Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat and said, “Because you became a friend of Ahaziah, the Lord has destroyed your work.” His ship was wrecked and could not go to Tarshish.
Jehoshaphat rested with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. His son Jehoram reigned in his place.
He had six brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Mishael, Shephatiah, and Azariahu. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold, and weapons, along with fortified cities in Judah. But he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.
Jehoram took his place in his kingdom and became strong. He killed all his brothers with the sword, along with some of the rulers of Israel.
He was thirty-two years old when he took his place in his kingdom, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, because Ahab's daughter was his wife. He did evil before the Lord.
But the Lord was unwilling to destroy the house of David because of the covenant he had made with David, and because he had promised to give him and his sons a lamp forever.
In those days Edom rebelled against Judah, and they set a king over themselves.
Jehoram went out with his commanders and all his cavalry. He rose during the night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots. The army fled to their homes.
Edom broke away from Judah's control and has remained so to this day. At that time Libnah also rebelled against his rule, because they had forsaken the Lord, the God of their fathers.
For he made high places for himself in the cities of Judah, led the inhabitants of Jerusalem into prostitution, and led Judah astray.

A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, “This is what the Lord, the God of your father David, says: Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

but have walked in the ways of the king of Israel and led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem into prostitution, as the house of Ahab practiced prostitution, and have killed your brothers, your father's sons, who were better than you,
the Lord will strike you with great blows among your people, and will strike your sons, your wives, and all your possessions.
You yourself will waste away with a severe illness, a disease of the bowels, until your bowels come out because of the illness, day after day.”
The Lord stirred up against Jehoram the Philistines, the Arabs, and those who lived near the Ethiopians.

They came up against Judah and plundered it. They carried away all the goods they found in the king's house, along with his sons and daughters. No son remained to him except Ahaziah alone, the youngest of his sons.
After all this, the Lord struck him with a disease of the bowels for which there was no cure.

And as the days passed, when his time came, within two days his intestines came out because of the disease, and he died of that terrible illness. The people did not give him a funeral like the funerals of his fathers.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He died without honor and was buried in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, because the raiding band of Arabs and Alimazonians that had come against them had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram king of Judah, became king.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri.
He followed the ways of the house of Ahab, because his mother advised him to sin.
He did evil before the Lord, as the house of Ahab had done, because after his father's death they became his advisers, bringing about his destruction.
Following their advice, he went with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, and the archers wounded Jehoram.

Jehoram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Syrians had inflicted on him at Ramoth when he fought against Hazael king of Syria. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was ill.
Ahaziah's downfall came from the Lord through his journey to Jehoram. When he went there, he went out to Jehu son of Amasa, the Lord's anointed.
When Jehu took vengeance on the house of Ahab, he also found the officials of Judah and Ahaziah's brothers, who served Ahaziah, and killed them.

He ordered them to search for Ahaziah. They captured him while he was recovering in Samaria, brought him to Jehu, and Jehu killed him. They buried him there, because they said, "He is a son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart." There was no one in Ahaziah's house who could be strengthened to exercise royal power.
When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw that her son was dead, she rose up and destroyed all the royal offspring in the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and secretly removed him from among the king's sons who were being killed. She put him and his nurse in the bedrooms. Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the sister of Ahaziah and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, hid him and concealed him from Athaliah, so that she did not kill him.
He remained hidden with her in the house of God for six years, while Athaliah ruled over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and brought the commanders of hundreds—Azariah son of Jehoram, Ishmael son of Jonah, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zechariah—into the house of the Lord.
They traveled throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, along with the heads of the families of Israel, and came to Jerusalem.

They made a covenant with the whole assembly of Judah in the house of the Lord and with the king. He showed them the king's son and said to them, "Here is the son of the king of Judah. He shall reign, as the Lord said concerning the house of David."
Now this is what you shall do: a third of you, the priests and Levites, shall come in for Sabbath duty at the entrances of the gates.
A third shall be in the king's house, and a third at the middle gate. All the people shall be in the courtyard of the house of the Lord.

And let no one enter the house of the Lord except the priests, the Levites, and the ministers from among the Levites. They may enter because they are holy, and all the people must observe the requirements of the Lord.
And the Levites shall surround the king, each man with his weapon in his hand. Whoever enters the house shall die, and they shall be with the king when he enters and when he leaves.
And the Levites and all Judah did everything that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each man took his companion at the beginning of the Sabbath, because Jehoiada had not dismissed the regular guards.
And he gave them the swords, shields, and weapons that had belonged to King David and were in the house of God.
He stationed all the people, each with his own weapon, from the right side of the house to the left side, beside the altar and the temple, all around the king.
And he brought out the king’s son and placed the crown and the testimony upon him. They made him king, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, “Long live the king!”
And Athaliah heard the sound of the people running, giving thanks, and praising the king, and she entered the house of the Lord to come to the king.

She looked, and there was the king standing in his place at the entrance to the passage, with the leaders, trumpeters, and rulers around the king. All the people were rejoicing, blowing trumpets, singing songs with musical instruments, and offering praises. Athaliah tore her garment, cried out, and said, “You are acting treacherously!”

And Jehoiada the priest went out. Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds and the leaders of the army, saying to them, “Take her outside the house, and go out after her. Let her die by the sword.” For the priest had said, “She must not die in the house of the Lord.”
And they let her go, and she passed through the Horsemen’s Gate of the king’s house, and they killed her there.
And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, the people, and the king, that they would be the Lord’s people.
And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and demolished it. They smashed his altars and his idols, and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, before his altar.

And Jehoiada the priest placed the work of the house in the hands of the Levitical priests. He appointed the regular ministers, the priests and the Levites whom David had set apart for the house of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with joy and songs under David’s direction.
And the gatekeepers stood at the gates of the house of the Lord, and no one who was unclean in any respect entered there.

And he took the heads of the clans, the warriors, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land. They brought the king out of the house of the Lord and entered the king’s house through the inner gate, and seated the king on the royal throne.
And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. And they killed Athaliah with the sword.
Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
And Joash did what was right before the Lord throughout the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Joash took two wives for himself and fathered sons and daughters.
And after this, Joash took it into his heart to restore the house of the Lord.

And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and collect silver from all Israel to strengthen the house of the Lord year by year, and hurry to speak.” But the Levites did not believe.

And King Joash called Jehoiada the chief and said to him, “Why did you not see to it that the Levites brought in from Judah and Jerusalem what had been prescribed by Moses, the man of God? For he assembled Israel at the tent of testimony.”
For Athaliah was lawless, and her sons demolished the house of God. They also used the holy things of the house of God for the Baals.
And the king said, “Let there be a chest, and let it be placed outside, at the entrance to the house of the Lord.”
And let them proclaim in Judah and Jerusalem that people should bring an offering to the Lord, as Moses, the servant of the God of Israel, had commanded in the wilderness.
And all the leaders and all the people gave, bringing their offerings in and putting them into the chest until it was full.

Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king’s overseers, and they saw that the money had increased, the king’s chief scribe and the high priest’s overseer would come and empty the chest, then put it back in its place. They did this day after day and collected a great deal of money.
And the king and Jehoiada the priest gave it to those who carried out the work of restoring the house of the Lord. They hired stonecutters and carpenters to repair the house of the Lord.
And they carried out the work, and the work prospered in their hands. They restored the house of the Lord to its proper condition and strengthened it.

When they had finished, they brought the remaining money to the king and to Jehoiada. They made utensils for the house of the Lord, equipment for the service of burnt offerings, and incense burners of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually throughout all the days of Jehoiada.
And Jehoiada grew old, full of days, and died at the age of one hundred and thirty.
When he died, they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good toward Israel, toward God, and toward his house.
After Jehoiada’s death, the leaders of Judah came in and bowed down to the king, and they changed Joash’s mind. Then the king listened to them.
They abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers, and served idols and the Ashtoreths. And the Lord’s anger came upon Judah and Jerusalem in those days.
And he sent prophets to them to bring them back to the Lord, but they did not listen. He gave them a warning, but they did not heed it.

And the Spirit of the Lord clothed Azariah, the son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood up among all the people and said, “Thus says the Lord: Why have you turned away from the Lord’s commandments? You will not prosper, because you have abandoned the Lord, and he will abandon you.”
And they rose against him and stoned him at the command of King Joash in the courtyard of the house of the Lord.
Joash did not remember the kindness that Jehoiada, his father, had shown him, but killed his son. As he was dying, he said, “May the Lord see and judge.”
At the end of that year, the Syrian army came up against him and invaded Judah and Jerusalem. They killed all the leaders of the people in the army and sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus.

For the Syrian army came with only a few men, but God delivered a very large army into their hands, because they had abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers. And he carried out judgment against Joash.

After they departed from him, leaving him gravely ill, his servants rose against him because of the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest. They killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in the city of David, but did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
Those who rose against him were Zabad, the son of Shimeath the Ammonite, and Jehozabad, the son of Shimrith the Moabite.
And all his sons [?], and five came to him, and they laid many supplies upon him. And the rest of the acts of Joash are written in the book of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Jehoaddin, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the sight of the Lord, but not with his whole heart.
When the kingdom was firmly established in his hands, he killed his servants who had killed the king, his father.

But he did not kill their sons, in keeping with the covenant of the Lord’s law, as it is written and as the Lord commanded, saying, “Fathers shall not die for their sons, and sons shall not die for their fathers; rather, each person shall die for his own sins.”

Amaziah gathered the house of Judah and appointed commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds for them according to their ancestral households throughout Judah and Jerusalem. He counted those twenty years old and above and found three hundred thousand warriors who went out to battle carrying spears and shields.
He hired a hundred thousand mighty warriors from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.
A man of God came to him and said, “King, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the Lord is not with Israel or with any of the sons of Ephraim.
If you think you will gain strength through them, the Lord will deliver you to defeat before your enemies, for it is the Lord who gives strength and brings defeat.”
Amaziah said to the man of God, “What shall I do about the hundred talents I gave to the army of Israel?” The man of God said to him, “The Lord can give you more than that.”
Amaziah dismissed the troops who had come to him from Ephraim, telling them to return to their own place. They became very angry with Judah and returned to their own places in anger and fury.
